symptom: ako/mxcli#1777 (follow-up to #1769): `alter microflow … { insert after $Related begin change $First (Status = 'Seen'); end; }` with $First = head $Lines in the stored flow was refused, nothing written: "cannot qualify member \"Status\": the entity its variable holds is not known here". The same for any member (find/filter by, sort, change) of a stored filter/sort/tail/union/intersect/subtract/range/head/find output, a Java action result (entity, list, list of a type parameter), or a retrieve over a self-reference. `create microflow` types all of them.
cause: alterFlowContext.storedVariables, the scope a spliced fragment starts from, left ListOperationAction, JavaActionCallAction and a self-reference AssociationRetrieveSource 'Unknown'; associationRetrieveType returned "" for a self-reference because 'which end it starts from is not known'.
file: mdl/executor/cmd_alter_flow.go (storedVariables, storedDependent, storedDependents.typeOf), mdl/executor/cmd_microflows_builder_actions.go (listOperationResult, listResult.typeFrom, listOperationInput, aggregateResultType, associationRetrieveType), mdl/executor/cmd_microflows_builder_calls.go (javaActionResultType, returnsTypeParameterList, firstListType, javaActionArgVariables)
fix: The full build's typing was pulled out of addListOperationAction, addAggregateListAction and addCallJavaActionAction into functions over the stored shapes (the microflows.ListOperation, the AggregateFunction + ReduceReturnType, the JavaAction definition + argument variables), and storedVariables calls the same ones: a list operation's output and a Java action's result are storedDependents typed in the fixed point, so one reading a list another output holds is typed whatever the stored order, and a name two origins give different derivations stays untyped (a head and a find of one list are one origin). Aggregates get the primitive the full build declares. A self-reference is followed from its FROM end.
test: mdl/executor/flow_splice_stored_outputs_test.go (TestStoredVariables_ListOperationJavaAndSelfReferenceAreTyped, TestSpliceFragment_MembersOfStoredOutputsAreQualified: 13 shapes, TestSpliceFragment_MembersOfConflictingOutputsAreRefused); flow_splice_assoc_retrieve_test.go $Parent now Mod.Order. Controls: storedVariables and associationRetrieveType reverted -> all 12 new shapes refused 'cannot qualify member' (the self reference set was already typed); conflict guard off -> $Dup typed Mod.Tag, $Mixed Mod.OrderLine, both written. Platform 11.13.0: 7 alters refused before, all 8 written after, mx check 0 errors, describe -> exec Unchanged.
insight: The stored AssociationRetrieveSource has no direction field (only StartVariableName and the association), so 'which end a self-reference starts from' is not a missing fact to be guessed but a platform rule to be measured: on 11.13.0 `retrieve $P from $Order/M.Order_Parent; change $P (…)` builds and `count($P)` is CE0013 "Input variable 'P' must be of type 'List'" — Mendix follows it from the FROM end. Owner Both on a self-reference is CE0002, so that case does not exist. The full build types a self-reference by use (a list unless an object use follows), which disagrees with the platform for a list use; the fragment takes the platform's reading. To type stored outputs, refactor the builder's typing to take the stored action rather than the AST statement, then call it from both sides — the builder's switch on ast.ListOpX was the only copy and would have drifted.
